item.content:encoded:
November 19, 2026, has long been circled on your calendar. Birthdays, anniversaries, and holidays have come and gone, but this day belongs to you and your XBOX console. We can hardly believe it’s almost here, either. Once midnight strikes, you want to be locked in the action, so to help you prepare, we created a checklist to ensure distractions are put to bed so you can settle in for a season of gaming like nothing you’ve ever experienced before.

Make Some Hard (Drive) Choices

2026 has been full of some absolute bangers: Gears of War E-Day, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, Forza Horizon 6, Halo: Campaign Evolved, Minecraft Dungeons II, Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred, Control Resonant, Mixtape, Pragmata, The Blood of Dawnwalker,  Star Wars: Galactic Racer, 007 First Light, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve… seriously, all these games came out this year. That also means you might have a hard drive that is nearing capacity. And you will be faced with some hard choices to free up approximately 212GB of space on your XBOX Series X|S before November 19.

You could always upgrade the capacity of your console to keep all your games at the ready, using the storage expansion slot on the back of the console. Otherwise, you’ll have a hard choice to make which we do not envy. But know that you’re in good company – we had to find a way to make room too.

Connect to the Cloud

XBOX Cloud Gaming means that you don’t need to own an XBOX Series X|S console to experience the latest games (or use up that hard drive space) – you can stream directly from the cloud to your XBOX One console. Game Pass subscribers receive an allotment of hours per month as part of their plans, but you can also purchase blocks of time. Certain upcoming major releases have been confirmed as cloud-ready on day one, so even if you don’t own a current gen console, your latest obsession isn’t out of reach.

Ready Your Console

You never want to settle in for a long gaming session only to immediately get hit with an update download. If you haven’t used your XBOX Series X|S or XBOX One in a minute, be sure to power up and connect to the internet beforehand and make sure you’re all set with the latest system updates. You can also install any upcoming releases you may have pre-ordered, while you’re at it.

Call in Sick

If you’re feeling a gaming flu coming on (and there’s a lot of that going around right now), then take a sick day, rather than risk infecting your coworkers or classmates. Sometimes you just need to listen to your body’s needs, relax, and let the fever run its course. Miami’s own DJ Khaled, aka Dr. XBOX will write you a personalized note to help explain the situation. If this thing is really serious, you may even need the whole week to recover – it’s the responsible thing to do.

Hire a Dog Walker

We all have responsibilities. Some of them come with four legs and a suspect bladder. Don’t let Rufus ruin your gaming fun. Get ahold of a local dog walker to take them outside so you can enjoy the big day uninterrupted. Or drop them off at doggie daycare for a day (or week) to get them out of your hair.

Reconsider Placement of Your XBOX

Is your XBOX in an area of the house that is easily accessible to younger players? Consider the steps you need to take to get it out of younger sightlines, like running an extension cable out to the shed in the backyard or huddling up in your at-home office. Even if you do find yourself bouncing between rooms, your save files reside in the Cloud, allowing you to pick up your session wherever you last plugged your console in.

Update Your Playlist

We’re always on the hunt for new tunes and one of the things we’re most looking forward to on November 19 is discovering a whole bunch of new tracks that are sure to make our listening playlist pop throughout the year. You can get started here on Spotify.

Create a New XBOX Wireless Controller to Commemorate the Day

XBOX Design Lab lets you create your own next-gen XBOX Wireless Controller. Choose from a combination of colors, patterns, textured grips, and more. You could even pick up some specially themed versions of controllers styled in hot pink and pastels – this one is particularly striking.

Charge Your Controller

Speaking of controllers, if you expect long gaming sessions in your near future, make sure that it’s plugged in so it has a full charge when you need it, or stock up on AA batteries. Maybe even get a backup controller ready so you can hot-swap them in and minimize interruptions.

Prepare for a Tale of Two Tragic Lovers in Crime

Looking for something to add to your queue? Check out the 1967 classic, “Bonnie and Clyde,” featuring Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway to get you in the mood for an epic story about two tragic lovers who fall into a life of crime. We’ll have to wait and see if the outcome is any different this time around starting on November 19.

Watch Out for Gators

No seriously, we saw one recently.

item.title: Millions of Butt Slaps: Last Pirates Sails into XBOX Game Preview
item.dc:creator: john sherwood, 3rd Party Product Specialist
item.description:

The post Millions of Butt Slaps: Last Pirates Sails into XBOX Game Preview appeared first on XBOX Wire.
item.content:encoded:
Summary

  • Online co-op comedy horror game for up to four players.
  • Out now in XBOX Game Preview with Steam crossplay.
  • The story of how it got here and what’s next.

Ahoy, pirates! We’re RetroStyle Games, a team from Kyiv, Ukraine, and our online co-op horror game Last Pirates: Die Together is out today in XBOX Game Preview on XBOX Series X|S and PC. It has crossplay with Steam! So, a lobby can be half on console and half on PC and still lose their butts together.

Up to four pirates land on a cursed island, grab treasure with stretchy arms and drag it back to the ship before the captain’s quota runs out. In practice monsters flip the cart, a monkey begs for coins (bro, we’re broke too), and somebody always wants to tear off a friend’s booty and slap it.

Honestly, we had no idea what to write here. We’ve never done anything like this before. Making a game is a thousand small stories, and they won’t fit into 1,000 words. We could just write “butt” a thousand times, but we’d rather share a few favorites, so you get to know the crew behind the booty.

Story 1: The Game Jam that Got out of Hand

After Ocean Keeper, our pretty serious roguelike, we wanted something much lighter, so in January, 2026 we ran a game jam inside the studio. Once the pirate prototype was playable, the office never got quiet again. Why pirates? Yarr, who doesn’t love pirates?!

Story 2: The Playtest Where the Butt Came off

We wanted our pirates to be breakable, so at zero health they snap in half. In one playtest everybody kept trying to stick the bottom half back on, so we coded it, and the revive worked better than anything we had planned. Now monsters bite butts off, crewmates steal them, and a downed pirate comes back when a friend slaps a spare booty onto them.

For Steam Next Fest in June we put a giant butt on the beach and asked players to slap it a million times to unlock an update. An average pirate lands about 1,000 slaps in five hours, so we expected it to take a while. But(t)… one crew of four did it alone in seven hours. We were not prepared.

Story 3: The Mimic Learns to Talk

For a long time the Mimic was our most boring monster: it only copied how a player looked, and we could spot it every time. Then streamers walked straight up to it, sure it was their buddy. Okay, the Mimic works. Time to make it worse. Now each Mimic picks any player in the lobby, copies their skin and borrows short shouts from their voice chat. Two Mimics on the map? Two pirates in the crew have evil twins. Today it’s our favorite monster (not counting the muscle-mice, they’re number one).

Story 4: Our Favorite Bug, and Other Things Players Found that we Never Made

Every streamer we’ve played with does the same two things on their first spawn: slaps a butt, then climbs into the cauldron and flies off the map, thanks to a bug they all find within seconds. Maybe we were all witches in a past life. The cauldron still flies, and we’re keeping it.

Then a group on YouTube snuck up behind our monster who only moves when nobody’s looking (we call him Misha, short for Man In Shdows), sniffed his butt, and he vanished. Pure coincidence, but they were sure it was a secret mechanic and kept sniffing him for the rest of the video. It “worked” two times out of three. There’s no such mechanic, and it was so funny to watch.

Story 5: A Bowling Prophecy

We also dreamed of a certain YouTuber playing it, the one the internet pictures as a bag of milk in a propeller hat. One night the marketing team went bowling and made a bet: if each of us rolled a strike in a row, we’d email him. We all did. The email with the subject line “Bowling prophecy” went out, he answered, and he actually played Last Pirates. We’re still not over it.

Story 6: Kyiv

Some days the meeting moves to the shelter, or a playtest runs on the generator during blackouts. One morning a strike hit across the road, bent our windows inward and injured one of our teammates. That’s the scary reality for everyone who lives in Ukraine. It doesn’t stop us: this team and this silly pirate game keep us sane, and we want to bring a little joy. If people get scared, let it be of Misha or a jump scare and nothing else. We are so grateful to everyone who makes it possible for us to keep making games in Kyiv.

Current Port: XBOX, and We’re Not Stopping

On XBOX the game gets the same updates as Steam at the same time, and crews can mix both platforms. A new event is coming this winter, and after that, the full release.

What’s in XBOX Game Preview

• Online co-op for one to four players, with Steam crossplay.

• Optimized for XBOX Series X|S.

• XBOX Play Anywhere: buy once, play on XBOX Series X|S and PC.

• In-game voice chat (the Mimic says thanks).

• A lobby browser to find a crew.

• Meta-progression: weapons, items and a wardrobe full of skins.

• Regular updates in sync with Steam.

See you on the Islands

Last Pirates: Die Together is out now in XBOX Game Preview. Grab friends, slap booty, set sail and let us know what you think! Thank you from the bottom of our hearts.

P.S. Butt, butt, butt. It would be a sin not to use this chance, hehe.

This game is a work in progress. It may or may not change over time or release as a final product. Purchase only if you are comfortable with the current state of the unfinished game. Grab your crew, grab the loot, and try not to lose your butt. Literally. Last Pirates: Die Together is a comedic online co-op adventure for up to 4 players. You and your crew use wobbly, stretchy arms to haul as much treasure as possible back to your captain. Break down doors, snatch every coin in sight, and survive the monsters, the traps, and each other's terrible decisions along the way. Every run drops you onto a mysterious island full of cursed loot and lurking creatures. Team up, make a plan, and shout over voice chat. Just make sure at least one of you makes it back to the ship with the gold. Be a hero, hide like a coward, or "accidentally" volunteer a teammate as a distraction. They will be fine. Probably. Expect chaotic physics and voice-morphing mayhem. And the butts do more than revive your crew: each one grants its own buff that shakes up how you play. It is loud, it is messy, and it is best played with friends. Round up your crew. Grab the treasure. Make it a story worthy of a shanty. Full details on the latest status of the game, how you can give feedback and report issues can be found at https://discord.gg/YywWVj4jJK
